subject: maths
question: A baker sells 100 cupcakes and earns a profit equal to the selling price of 20 cupcakes. What is his profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When profit is equal to the Selling Price (SP) of x items for n items sold:

Profit % = [x ÷ (n − x)] × 100

Profit % = [20 ÷ (100 − 20)] × 100

Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%

In decimal form: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total cupcakes sold = 100, Profit = SP of 20 cupcakes.

Formula: Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

 Total Selling Price (100 units) 
• Cost Price (80 units) Profit (20 units) 
• Base for % Calculation (CP) 

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 cupcake = 1 unit.

⇒ Total SP of 100 cupcakes = 100 units.

⇒ Profit = SP of 20 cupcakes = 20 units.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit

⇒ CP = 100 − 20 = 80 units.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%.

⇒ Profit in decimal = 0.25.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit based on Cost Price

If profit is equal to the CP of x items while selling n items, then Profit % = (x ÷ n) × 100.

Loss based on Selling Price

If loss is equal to the SP of x items while selling n items, then Loss % = [x ÷ (n + x)] × 100.

Marked Price (MP)

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Selling Price = MP × [1 − (Discount % ÷ 100)].
